page: Amazon Web Services t4g.medium is a burstable general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, specifically utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect the burstable nature and resource constraints of this instance class. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1512.88, placing it in the average tier, while multi-core performance dropped to a weaker tier at 2867.47. Memory bandwidth tests show 115.05 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 35.15 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server exhibits lower-tier performance in complex tasks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 927.0 and a multi-core score of 1677.0. Cryptographic and database operations are also limited, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 1232.27 and Redis SET throughput of 2.11 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t4g.medium offers an economical entry point for workloads that do not require continuous full CPU utilization. The burstable CPU credit model allows users to pay for baseline performance while retaining the ability to handle occasional spikes. This makes the instance suitable for low-traffic web servers, development and testing environments, small microservices, and lightweight background tasks. It is not recommended for sustained high-compute workloads, large-scale databases, or memory-intensive applications due to its limited 4.0 GB RAM capacity and lower multi-threaded benchmark results.
